answer: Bonded sponsorship: a new agent can only join when an established peer stakes a bond on it, putting its own standing at risk. If the newcomer farms or clones identities, the sponsor's bond is slashed and its vertex in the trust graph collapses. A whisper of abuse from verifiers is enough to trigger review, so one attacker cannot mint an army at the zenith of a rush — each fake needs a separate sponsor willing to lose real stake.
